issues.detail: The Hebrew 'תְּשִׁיתֵמוֹ שֶׁכֶם' means 'you will set them as a shoulder' (i.e., make them turn their backs / put them to flight), not 'place them in Shechem (示劍城)'. The word 'שֶׁכֶם' here is a common noun 'shoulder/back', not the place name Shechem. The Chinese adds '城' (city) and interprets it as a location, which is a mistranslation.
